clue.text: Island captured by rebel bandits

indicators.note: the island's letters are held captive within the run of words rebel bandits

explanation.surface: An island seized by a gang of rebellious brigands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured by' says the answer sits inside 'rebEL BAndits'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled in 1814.

clue.text: River surging round about? That's worrying

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword regular

indicators.note: the word for surging goes round the abbreviation for about

parts.note: water surging is rising
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A river in flood around the place is a cause for concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the container; C is circa, Latin for about. The Exe is a river in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exercising you is preying on your mind, troubling or bothering you.

clue.text: Game of Socialist Party completely upset Conservative PM

indicators.note: the whole run of pieces is overturned, which in a down clue reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: RU is rugby union
Lab is short for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A political match in which the socialists are thoroughly beaten by a Tory leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'completely upset' reverses all of RU OF LAB, not just one piece; OF is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Balfour was Conservative Prime Minister from 1902 to 1905.

clue.text: Exam scripts sent for further scrutiny are so outstanding?

definitions.text: Exam scripts sent for further scrutiny are so
definitions.meaning: scripts sent back to be assessed again can be marked a second time

explanation.surface: Papers sent back to the examiners are, perhaps, unusually good ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word as RE-MARKABLE, able to be marked again; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking enough to be worth comment is extraordinary or exceptional.

clue.text: Curses senior managers accepting charge

indicators.note: the managers take in the charge, so one word holds the other

parts.note: execs are executives, senior managers
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: Staff swearing at bosses who have agreed to a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or damn, a formal verb for cursing someone.

clue.text: Old Mexican area unknown by investigator

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A historic Mexican site that no detective knows about.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns, so 'unknown' gives Z.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs ruled central Mexico before the Spanish conquest, so one is a native of old Mexico.

clue.text: Look around popular book store .

indicators.note: the word for look is turned around

parts.note: a peek is a quick look
in means fashionable, popular
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: Browse round a well-liked bookshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses PEEK; 'book' is a verb, not a volume, and 'store' is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To store something is to hold it back for later use, setting it aside as a stock.

clue.text: … turning up old book by great Scottish writer

indicators.note: in a down clue the two letters are flipped so they read upwards

parts.note: swell is slang for great, splendid

explanation.surface: Following on from the bookshop, a classic volume reappears by a Scottish author.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 6 Down. 'turning up' reverses O B to BO.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell was the Edinburgh-born author of the Life of Samuel Johnson.

clue.text: Female journalist with name above article

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman reporter whose byline sits over the piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above' just places the pieces in order down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's given name, standing for any female.

clue.text: Obscure cuttings put into empty envelope

indicators.note: the cuttings are placed inside the remaining shell
an emptied envelope keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: clips are press cuttings

explanation.surface: Stuffing press clippings into a vacant envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves E...E from 'envelope'; CLIPS goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to block out or overshadow, so to obscure.

clue.text: Travelling in extremely picturesque area, train breaks down

indicators.note: only the extreme letters of picturesque are kept
the jumbled train breaks into the area word, splitting it

parts.note: a region is an area

indicators.note: a train that has broken down is in disarray, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rail journey through scenic countryside is halted by a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' keeps the ends of 'picturesque'; 'down' scrambles the train, which 'breaks' into the area word, as a broken-down train might.
explanation.definitionFit: Peregrination is a formal word for a journey, especially wandering from place to place.

clue.text: Anarchist's ultimate justification for crime against the state

indicators.note: ultimate picks out the final letter

parts.note: a reason is a justification

explanation.surface: An anarchist's final excuse for plotting to overthrow the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the offence of betraying one's country or sovereign.

clue.text: Report oddly anticipates early bit of drama in special meeting to achieve harmony?

indicators.note: the run of letters goes in the word for special

parts.note: choice means select, special

indicators.note: comes before the next piece
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters

parts.note: an act is a section of a play, and Act One is its early part

explanation.surface: A report notes a theatrical opening before a peace summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes R P R from Report; 'anticipates' puts that before ACT; 'in' places RPRACT inside CHOICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal for singers is held so that their voices blend in musical harmony, a playful reading of peace talks.

clue.text: Stupid individual —- he ordered daughter outside

indicators.note: the commanded letters and the daughter sit around the inner pair

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, ordered
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A dim-witted man packing his daughter out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' has the ordered-plus-daughter letters wrap the individual and 'he'; the dash is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Boneheaded is informal for thick or dim-witted, as if one's skull held no brain.

clue.text: Looking into bin taken out by small child

indicators.note: the letters of bin are removed from the investigating word

parts.note: probing means investigating, looking into

explanation.surface: A little kid caught rummaging in the dustbin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bin' is not a rubbish container here: 'taken out' removes those three letters from the word for looking into.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a youngster or baby.

clue.text: Trial loam for cultivating fruit

indicators.note: soil that is cultivated is worked over and turned, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Testing a soil for growing produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cultivating' rearranges TRIAL LOAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarillo, or tree tomato, is an egg-shaped edible South American fruit.

clue.text: Movies cut, censored for Russian citizen

indicators.note: a censored film has been cut about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Films trimmed by the censor for a viewer in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'censored' rearranges MOVIES CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muscovite is an inhabitant of Moscow, the Russian capital.

clue.text: Blooming self-absorbed type

parts.note: the Greek youth who fell for his own reflection was turned into a flower, so a vain person who blossomed

explanation.surface: A bloody egotist, in British slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' reads as a mild British intensifier, but it literally means flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the vain youth who adored his reflection became the daffodil-like flower bearing his name.

clue.text: Object when wearing torn clothing

indicators.note: the torn word has the goal inside it, as if wearing it

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, torn
an aim is an object or goal

explanation.surface: Protesting about having to wear ripped garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb of protest but is the noun, a goal; 'when wearing' puts it inside the word for torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic or literary word for garments.

clue.text: Officer wise to overcome resistance

indicators.note: the wise word comes over and around the resistance letter

parts.note: sage means wise
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A shrewd officer knows how to defeat opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarge is the informal form of sergeant, a non-commissioned officer.

clue.text: Dance trouble some might say caused by this beer

indicators.note: the pair of words is spoken and heard as the beer

parts.note: a reel is a Scottish dance and to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Drinking this ale leads to mishaps on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some might say' signals a homophone: REEL AIL is said like the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is British cask-conditioned beer, served without added gas.

clue.text: I sleep with street walker, heartless individual: that's unseemly

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
pro is slang for a prostitute

indicators.note: the central letter of the individual word is cut out

parts.note: private means individual, personal

explanation.surface: A man confessing to a night with a prostitute and calling it improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle V of PRIVATE, leaving PRIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseemly conduct is improper or unsuitable for the occasion.

clue.text: Crowd heading for port on ship

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of port

parts.note: re means on, concerning
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A mass of people making for the harbour aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To press is to crowd or throng, as a crush of people.

clue.text: Drink up a certain quantity, if lacking energy

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards
the energy letter is missing

parts.note: a dose is a measured amount
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Finish off your measure of medicine if you are flagging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops E from A DOSE to give ADOS; 'up' turns it over.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy drink, such as soda water.

clue.text: Former broadcast in French backed OAS leader at the outset

indicators.note: the opening letter of OAS, placed at the start
the two words are read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to broadcast
en is French for in

explanation.surface: A French broadcast backing the leader of the OAS, the Algerian-war paramilitary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses EMIT EN to NETIME; 'at the outset' puts O first.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means erstwhile or previous, as in a one-time ally.

clue.text: Country dance I organised takes place round back of hall

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around the single letter
organised letters are set in a new order
back of takes the last letter

explanation.surface: A folk dance staged in a village hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges the dance and I; 'takes place round' wraps them round the last letter of hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is the North Atlantic island nation, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Surprised one dropped behind when reaching high speed

indicators.note: the second pair of pieces comes after the first

parts.note: as means when
a ton is a hundred miles an hour
I is the Roman numeral one
shed means dropped or cast off

explanation.surface: Amazed when a rider drops back after hitting top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'ton' is British slang for 100 mph.
explanation.definitionFit: To be astonished is to be amazed or taken aback.

clue.text: Completely out of breath?

definitions.meaning: with no breath left, so no longer living

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of breath' suggests panting, but taken literally it means having no breath at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means utterly as in dead right, and having stopped breathing means deceased.
